questions.question: Which tissue is responsible for movement in our body?

• Smooth muscle tissue is found in walls of internal organs such as the stomach, intestines, and blood vessels and is responsible for involuntary movements.

• Epithelial tissue forms the lining of internal and external surfaces of the body, including skin and the lining of organs.
 
• It provides protection and is involved in absorption, secretion, and sensation.
 
 
 
• **Connective tissue**

questions.question: The magnification produced by a spherical mirror is +0.75. The image is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Virtual, erect and diminished**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The magnification produced by a spherical mirror is given as +0.75.
 
• A positive magnification indicates that the image is virtual and erect.
 
• The magnification value (0.75) is less than 1, indicating that the image is diminished.
 
• Virtual images formed by spherical mirrors are always erect.
 
• Therefore, the image is virtual, erect, and diminished.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Concave Mirrors**

 
 
• Concave mirrors can produce both real and virtual images depending on the position of the object.
 
• When the object is placed between the focal point and the mirror, a virtual, erect, and enlarged image is formed.
 
 
 
• **Convex Mirrors**
 
 
• Convex mirrors always produce virtual, erect, and diminished images regardless of the object's position.
 
• These mirrors are commonly used as rear-view mirrors in vehicles.
 
 
 
• **Magnification Formula**
 
 
• The magnification (m) produced by a spherical mirror is given by the formula m = -v/u, where v is the image distance and u is the object distance.
 
• A positive value of magnification indicates a virtual and erect image, while a negative value indicates a real and inverted image.

questions.question: A gardener increases the area of his rectangular garden by increasing its length by 40% and decreasing its breadth by 20%. The area of the new garden is what percentage more than the area of the old garden?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the **Successive Percentage Change** formula: Net Change = x + y + (x × y)/100

Here, increase in length (x) = +40 and decrease in breadth (y) = −20

Net change in Area = 40 − 20 + [40 × (−20)] / 100

Net change in Area = 20 − 8 = 12%

**∴ The correct answer is 12%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Increase in **Length** = 40%

Decrease in **Breadth** = 20%

**Formula Used:**

Area of Rectangle = Length × Breadth

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b5b2cb7c5ab4c0deb89e17e109e70e246998bcf9b5942a51902ddc956fa8dc9b.png] 

⇒ Let the initial **Length** be 10 units and initial **Breadth** be 10 units.

⇒ Initial Area = 10 × 10 = 100 units²

⇒ New Length = 10 + (40% of 10) = 14 units

⇒ New Breadth = 10 − (20% of 10) = 8 units

⇒ New Area = 14 × 8 = 112 units²

⇒ Percentage change = [(New Area − Initial Area) / Initial Area] × 100

⇒ Percentage change = [(112 − 100) / 100] × 100 = 12%

**∴ The correct answer is 12%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a value is changed by x% and then by y%, the overall percentage change is given by [x + y + (xy/100)]%.

Area and Multipliers

Percentage changes can be solved using decimal multipliers. An increase of 40% is × 1.4 and a decrease of 20% is × 0.8. The result is 1.4 × 0.8 = 1.12, representing a 12% increase.

Product Stability Rule

If the product (Area) remains constant while one factor (Length) increases by x%, the other factor (Breadth) must decrease by [x / (100 + x)] × 100%.</p

questions.question: Consider a parallel combination of 2 resistors with resistances 4 Ω and 6 Ω. The equivalent resistance of the circuit is:
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**2.4Ω**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When resistors are connected in a **parallel combination**, the reciprocal of the equivalent resistance is the sum of the reciprocals of the individual resistances.
 
• The formula for the equivalent resistance in a parallel circuit is:

 **1/R_eq = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂**, where R₁ and R₂ are the resistances of the individual resistors.
 
• Here, the given resistances are **4Ω** and **6Ω**.
 
• Substitute the values into the formula:

 **1/R_eq = 1/4 + 1/6**.
 
• Find the least common denominator (LCD) of 4 and 6, which is **12**. Rewrite the fractions:

 **1/R_eq = 3/12 + 2/12 = 5/12**.
 
• Reciprocate the result to find the equivalent resistance:

 **R_eq = 12/5 = 2.4Ω**.
 
• Thus, the equivalent resistance of the parallel combination is **2.4Ω**.
 
• Parallel circuits are commonly used in **electrical systems** to ensure that the voltage across each component is the same and to reduce the overall resistance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• This value corresponds to the sum of the resistances **(4Ω + 6Ω)**, which is the formula for resistances in series, not parallel. This is incorrect in the context of the given question.

questions.question: All liquids and gases are:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**fluids**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• All liquids and gases are considered **fluids** because they can flow.
 
• Fluids do not have a fixed shape and they take the shape of their container.
 
• Unlike solids, fluids have the ability to deform continuously under an applied shear stress.
 
• The molecules in fluids are not as tightly packed as in solids, allowing them to move freely past one another.
 
• Fluids can be characterized by their viscosity, which is a measure of their resistance to flow.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Solids**

 
 
• Solids have a definite shape and volume because their molecules are tightly packed and only vibrate in place.
 
• They do not flow like fluids and are rigid in nature.
 
 
 
• **Semiconductors**
 
 
• Semiconductors are materials that have a conductivity between conductors (metals) and insulators (non-metals).
 
• They are used in electronic devices to control the flow of current.
 
 
 
• **Insulators**
 
 
• Insulators are materials that do not allow the flow of electric current easily.
 
• They are used to protect us from the harmful effects of electricity by preventing unwanted flow of current.

questions.question: What type of reaction takes place when a single reactant breaks down into simpler products?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Decomposition**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A decomposition reaction is a type of chemical reaction where a single compound breaks down into two or more simpler substances.
 
• It generally requires an input of energy in the form of heat, light, or electricity to break the chemical bonds.
 
• Decomposition reactions are the opposite of combination reactions, where simpler substances combine to form a more complex compound.
 
• Examples of decomposition reactions include the breakdown of water into hydrogen and oxygen and the breakdown of calcium carbonate into calcium oxide and carbon dioxide.
 
• These reactions are important in various industrial processes and in the decomposition of organic matter in natural environments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Combination Reaction**

 
 
• In a combination reaction, two or more reactants combine to form a single product.
 
• Example: The reaction of hydrogen and oxygen to form water.
 
 
 
• **Displacement Reaction**
 
 
• In a displacement reaction, one element replaces another element in a compound.
 
• Example: The reaction of zinc with hydrochloric acid to produce zinc chloride and hydrogen gas.
 
 
 
• **Double Displacement Reaction**
 
 
• In a double displacement reaction, the ions of two compounds exchange places in an aqueous solution to form two new compounds.
 
• Example: The reaction of sodium sulfate with barium chloride to form barium sulfate and sodium chloride.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of particles of matter?

options.text: Particles of matter have space between them.
Particles of matter are continuously moving.
Particles of matter attract each other.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Particles of matter are static.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Particles of matter are always in a state of continuous motion, hence they are not static.
 
• Particles of matter have spaces between them, which allows them to move and interact.
 
• The movement of particles is influenced by temperature; higher temperatures increase their kinetic energy and motion.
 
• Particles of matter attract each other due to intermolecular forces, which can vary in strength depending on the type of matter.
 
• The concept of matter being static contradicts the kinetic theory of matter which states that particles are always in motion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **States of Matter**

 
 
• Matter exists in different states: solid, liquid, and gas, each with distinct characteristics based on particle arrangement and movement.
 
• In solids, particles are closely packed and have limited movement. In liquids, they are less tightly packed and move more freely. In gases, particles move rapidly and are far apart.
 
 
 
• **Kinetic Theory of Matter**
 
 
• This theory explains that matter is made up of particles which are in constant motion.
 
• The energy of particles increases with temperature, affecting their state and behavior.
 
 
 
• **Intermolecular Forces**
 
 
• These are forces of attraction or repulsion between particles of matter.
 
• They play a crucial role in determining the physical properties of substances, such as boiling and melting points.

questions.question: Which of the following represents the ratio by mass of hydrogen to oxygen atoms (H:O) in a water molecule?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1:8**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A water molecule (H₂O) consists of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.
 
• The atomic mass of hydrogen is approximately 1 u (atomic mass unit), and the atomic mass of oxygen is approximately 16 u.
 
• Therefore, the total mass of the hydrogen atoms in a water molecule is 2 u (2 hydrogen atoms × 1 u).
 
• The mass of the oxygen atom in a water molecule is 16 u.
 
• The ratio by mass of hydrogen to oxygen atoms in a water molecule is thus 2:16, which simplifies to 1:8.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Water Molecule Structure**

 
 
• Water is a polar molecule, with the oxygen atom having a partial negative charge and the hydrogen atoms having partial positive charges.
 
• This polarity leads to hydrogen bonding between water molecules, which gives water its unique properties such as high surface tension and boiling point.
 
 
 
• **Hydrogen Bonding**
 
 
• Hydrogen bonds are weak bonds that form between the hydrogen atom of one water molecule and the oxygen atom of another water molecule.
 
• These bonds are responsible for many of water's unusual properties, including its high specific heat capacity and its role as a universal solvent.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Water**
 
 
• Water is essential for life, serving as a solvent, a temperature buffer, and a reactant in various biochemical processes.
 
• It is also used in numerous industrial applications, including cooling, cleaning, and as a raw material in chemical reactions.

questions.question: Two successive discounts of 10% and 5% are equivalent to a single discount of _____.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For two **successive discounts** x% and y%, the **single equivalent discount** is calculated as:

**Equivalent Discount** = (x + y − (x × y / 100))%

Here, x = 10 and y = 5.

⇒ Discount = (10 + 5 − (10 × 5 / 100))% = 15 − 0.5 = 14.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 14.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** First discount = 10%, Second discount = 5%.

**Formula Used:** Selling Price = Marked Price × (100 − d₁)/100 × (100 − d₂)/100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a3182716b03c53689ae1b0d00f6c6fbfa07dca98f1f0bbf4bf6b897f7a750d73.png] 

⇒ Let the **Marked Price** be 100 units.

⇒ Price after the first 10% discount = 100 − (10% of 100) = 100 − 10 = 90 units.

⇒ Price after the second 5% discount = 90 − (5% of 90) = 90 − 4.5 = 85.5 units.

⇒ **Total Discount** = 100 − 85.5 = 14.5 units.

⇒ **Equivalent Discount Percentage** = (14.5 / 100) × 100 = 14.5%.

**∴ The correct answer is 14.5%.**

Marked Price and Discount

questions.question: If a regular polygon has 65 diagonals, then the number of sides this polygon has is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a **regular polygon** with **n sides**, the number of **diagonals** is given by the formula: **n(n − 3) ÷ 2**.

⇒ n(n − 3) ÷ 2 = 65

⇒ n(n − 3) = 130

We need to find two factors of 130 that differ by 3.

⇒ 130 = 13 × 10

Comparing n(n − 3) with 13(10), we get **n = 13**.

**∴ The correct answer is 13 sides.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of **diagonals** in the **regular polygon** = 65.

**Formula Used:**

Number of diagonals in an **n-sided polygon** = n(n − 3) ÷ 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0b0417aa313b8cda1e3fd9d8bcdd2e8e685200a9377021a7cb40871fe4550e37.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 65 = n(n − 3) ÷ 2

⇒ 130 = n² − 3n

⇒ n² − 3n − 130 = 0

To solve this **quadratic equation**, we split the middle term:

⇒ n² − 13n + 10n − 130 = 0

⇒ n(n − 13) + 10(n − 13) = 0

⇒ (n − 13)(n + 10) = 0

Possible values for n are:

⇒ n = 13 or n = −10

Since the **number of sides** (n) cannot be negative, we take n = 13.

The polygon is a **Tridecagon** (a 13-sided polygon).

**∴ The correct answer is 13 sides.**

The sum of all **interior angles** of an n-sided polygon is (n − 2) × 180°. For a tridecagon, it is 11 × 180° = 1980°.

Sum of Exterior Angles

For any **convex polygon**, the sum of all **exterior angles** is always constant and equal to 360°.

questions.question: If a sum amounts to 2 (1)/(4)times the sum after 2 years on a certain rate of compound interest, compounded annually, then the rate of interest per annum is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For **Compound Interest** over **n years**, the ratio of **Amount (A)** to **Principal (P)** is given by (1 + r/100)ⁿ.

Here, A/P = 2 1/4 = 9/4 and n = 2 years.

To find the 1-year multiplier, take the **square root**: √(9/4) = 3/2.

Interest rate = (Multiplier − 1) × 100 = (3/2 − 1) × 100 = 1/2 × 100 = 50%.

**∴ The correct answer is 50%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Time (t)** = 2 years

**Amount (A)** = 2 1/4 × Principal (P) = 9/4 P

**Formula Used:**

A = P(1 + r/100)t

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/20c649db8e2acf26270a100e49305b584f3495b41ac3224ce0c1bb4a70245dd4.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 9/4 P = P(1 + r/100)²

⇒ 9/4 = (1 + r/100)²

⇒ √(9/4) = 1 + r/100

⇒ 3/2 = 1 + r/100

⇒ r/100 = 3/2 − 1

⇒ r/100 = 1/2

⇒ r = 100 / 2

⇒ r = 50%

**∴ The correct answer is 50%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest (CI)

CI is calculated on the principal amount and also on the accumulated interest of previous periods. CI = A − P.

Effective Rate for 2 Years

questions.question: If we add 1 to the numerator and subtract 1 from the denominator of a given fraction, it becomes 1. It becomes (2)/(3) if 1 is added to the denominator of the given fraction while the numerator is left unchanged. The positive difference of numerator and denominator of the fraction is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

From the first condition, adding 1 to the **numerator** and subtracting 1 from the **denominator** makes the fraction equal to 1.

This implies that the modified numerator and denominator are equal: **(x + 1) = (y − 1)**.

By rearranging, we get **y − x = 1 + 1 = 2**.

Since **y − x** represents the difference between the denominator and numerator, the result is obtained directly.

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Let the **numerator** of the fraction be **x** and the **denominator** be **y**. The original fraction is **x/y**.

**Given:**

Condition 1: (x + 1) / (y − 1) = 1

Condition 2: x / (y + 1) = 2/3

**Formula Used:**

Cross-multiplication of **linear equations** to find unknown variables.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e6b3f002073a2e9a4ddc8fea8d88b8c2b91e158ca22d879c82e38103289085ef.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ From Condition 1: x + 1 = y − 1

⇒ y − x = 2 → (Equation 1)

⇒ From Condition 2: 3 × x = 2 × (y + 1)

⇒ 3x = 2y + 2 → (Equation 2)

⇒ From Eq 1, substitute y = x + 2 in Eq 2:

⇒ 3x = 2(x + 2) + 2

⇒ 3x = 2x + 4 + 2

⇒ x = 6

⇒ Substituting x = 6 in Eq 1: y = 6 + 2 = 8

⇒ Positive difference = |x − y| = |6 − 8| = 2

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

**__Additional Information__**

Types of Fractions

A **proper fraction** has a numerator smaller than the denominator (e.g., 3/4). An **improper fraction** has a numerator larger than or equal to the denominator (e.g., 8/6).

Simplest Form

A fraction is in its **simplest form** when the numerator and denominator have no common factors other than 1. For example, 6/8 simplifies to 3/4.

Reciprocal of a Fraction

The **reciprocal** is found by interchanging the numerator and denominator. The reciprocal of x/y is y/x.</p

questions.question: A class of 30 students appeared in a test. The average score of 12 students is 80, and that of the rest is 75. What is the average score of the class?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **students** = 12 : (30 − 12) = 12 : 18 = **2 : 3**.

Using **deviation method**: Assume base average = 75.

Extra points from 2 parts = 2 × (80 − 75) = **+10**.

Net increase in average = 10 ÷ (2 + 3) = **2**.

Final **average score** = 75 + 2 = 77.

**∴ The correct answer is 77.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total **students** = 30

Number of **Group 1** students = 12, Average = 80

Number of **Group 2** students = 30 − 12 = 18, Average = 75

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a7f2fb34f8d0266ad360fefb7a191c5a710025ac6a007543f5790e134bbc4bb7.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Weighted Average = (n₁ × A₁ + n₂ × A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of scores of 12 students = 12 × 80 = 960

⇒ Sum of scores of remaining 18 students = 18 × 75 = 1350

⇒ Total sum of scores for 30 students = 960 + 1350 = 2310

⇒ Average score of the class = 2310 ÷ 30

⇒ Average score = 77

**∴ The correct answer is 77.**

**__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Formula

When two or more groups are combined, the combined average is calculated as Aw = Σ(nᵢ × aᵢ) ÷ Σnᵢ, where n is the number of items and a is the average.

Properties of Average

If every value in a set is increased or decreased by a constant **k**, the average also increases or decreases by **k**.

Combined Average with Ratio

If the number of elements in two groups are in ratio **x : y**, the combined average depends only on this ratio, not the absolute number of elements.</p

questions.question: From a point on the ground, the angles of elevation of the top and the bottom of a flag that is mounted on an 18 m high pole, are respectively 60° and 30°. The height of the flag is :
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

In **Height and Distance**, for a fixed base, the heights are proportional to **tan θ**.

For 30°, **Ratio** = 1 : √3 ⇒ **Pole Height** = 1 unit = 18 m.

For 60°, **Ratio** = √3 : 1. To equate the base, multiply by √3 ⇒ **Total Height** = 3 units.

**Flag Height** = **Total Height** − **Pole Height** = 3 units − 1 unit = 2 units.

Since 1 unit = 18 m, **Flag Height** = 2 × 18 m = 36 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 36 m.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Height of the **pole** (BT) = 18 m

Angle of elevation of **bottom of flag** (T) = 30°

Angle of elevation of **top of flag** (F) = 60°

**Formula Used:**

tan θ = **Perpendicular** / **Base**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/eaac2cb880c54f56ab4f96f9d1dcdb04511fafa9e43a0a591367a1d7d673c955.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let **PB** be the distance from the point on the ground to the pole, and **h** be the height of the flag (TF).

⇒ In ▵TBP, tan 30° = BT / PB

⇒ 1 / √3 = 18 / PB

⇒ PB = 18√3 m

⇒ In ▵FBP, tan 60° = FB / PB

⇒ √3 = (BT + TF) / PB

⇒ √3 = (18 + h) / 18√3

⇒ 18√3 × √3 = 18 + h

⇒ 18 × 3 = 18 + h

⇒ 54 = 18 + h

⇒ h = 54 − 18 = 36 m

**∴ The correct answer is 36 m.**

**__Additional Information__**

Angle of Elevation

The angle between the **horizontal line** and the **line of sight** when looking up at an object.

Tangent Relation in Heights

For two objects on the same vertical line, **h₁/h₂ = tan θ₁/tan θ₂** when measured from the same point on the ground.

Complementary Angles

If the angles of elevation from two points at distances 'a' and 'b' are **complementary**, the height of the tower is **H = √(ab)**.</p

questions.question: Magnetic field lines around a straight current carrying conductor look like:
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Magnetic field lines around a straight current-carrying conductor form **concentric circles**.
 
• The direction of these magnetic field lines can be determined using the **Right-Hand Rule**.
 
• As the distance from the conductor increases, the spacing between the concentric circles increases, indicating that the magnetic field strength decreases.
 
• The magnetic field lines are **perpendicular** to the current-carrying conductor.
 
• This phenomenon is described by **Ampere's Circuital Law**, which relates the magnetic field around a conductor to the current passing through it.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Magnetic fields are produced by electric currents, which can be macroscopic currents in wires, or microscopic currents associated with electrons in atomic orbits.
 
 
 
• **Electromagnetism**
 
 
• Electromagnetism is a branch of physics involving the study of the electromagnetic force, a type of physical interaction that occurs between electrically charged particles.
 
• It encompasses various phenomena such as electricity, magnetism, and light.
 
 
 
• **Faraday's Law of Induction**
 
 
• Faraday's Law states that a change in the magnetic field within a closed loop induces an electromotive force (EMF) in the wire.

• Carbon's tetravalency allows it to bond with various elements, including hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, and sulfur, further expanding the range of possible organic molecules.

__
 
• The release of energy in the aerobic process is significantly greater than in the anaerobic process.
 
• ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate) is broken down to release a fixed amount of energy which can drive the endothermic reactions taking place in the cell.
 
• Pyruvate, a three-carbon molecule, is converted into lactic acid, which is also a three-carbon molecule during anaerobic respiration.
 
• In aerobic respiration, glucose is fully oxidized to carbon dioxide and water, producing a high yield of ATP.

• This is a set of metabolic reactions and processes that take place in the cells of organisms to convert biochemical energy from nutrients into ATP.

• It is the first step in both aerobic and anaerobic respiration, taking place in the cytoplasm of the cell.
 
• Glycolysis breaks down glucose into two molecules of pyruvate, yielding a net gain of two ATP molecules.
 
 
 
• **Fermentation**
 
 
• It is an anaerobic process by which cells generate energy through the conversion of glucose to lactic acid or ethanol.
 
• Fermentation allows cells to produce ATP without oxygen, though it is much less efficient compared to aerobic respiration.

• The length of the carbon chain can influence the physical properties of the compound, such as solubility and boiling point, but the functional group is more critical in determining chemical reactivity.

questions.question: What happens when pea plants showing two different characteristics (the tall/short trait and the round seed/wrinkled seed trait), rather than just one are bred with each other?

options.text: The tall/short trait and the round seed/wrinkled seed trait are independently inherited.
They are all tall and have round seeds in F2 generation.
Some F1 progeny are tall plants with round seeds, and some are short plants with wrinkled seeds.
The tall/short trait and the round seed/wrinkled seed trait are dependently inherited.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The tall/short trait and the round seed/wrinkled seed trait are independently inherited.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When pea plants showing two different characteristics are bred, each trait is inherited independently of the other.
 
• This observation is consistent with Mendel's Law of Independent Assortment, which states that alleles of different genes assort independently of one another during gamete formation.
 
• The F1 progeny will all be heterozygous, exhibiting the dominant traits for both characteristics.
 
• In the F2 generation, a 9:3:3:1 phenotypic ratio is typically observed, showing independent assortment.
 
• This means that the combination of traits can vary, resulting in plants that may be tall with round seeds, tall with wrinkled seeds, short with round seeds, or short with wrinkled seeds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Law of Segregation**

 
 
• Mendel's first law states that the two alleles for a heritable character segregate (separate) during gamete formation and end up in different gametes.
 
• This law ensures that offspring acquire one allele from each parent for each trait.
 
 
 
• **Law of Dominance**
 
 
• According to this law, in a heterozygote, one trait will conceal the presence of another trait for the same characteristic.
 
• The dominant allele is expressed in the phenotype, while the recessive allele is masked in the presence of the dominant allele.
 
 
 
• **Monohybrid Cross**
 
 
• A cross between individuals focusing on a single trait, which illustrates the inheritance of one characteristic.
 
• It typically results in a 3:1 phenotypic ratio in the F2 generation.

questions.question: The sum of five consecutive numbers is 260. The sum of the first and the last numbers is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

In a set of **consecutive numbers**, the **Average** is always the middle term.

Average = Total Sum ÷ Number of terms = 260 ÷ 5 = 52

For any set of numbers in **Arithmetic Progression**, the sum of the 1st and last terms is equal to twice the average.

Sum of first and last = 2 × Average = 2 × 52 = 104

**∴ The correct answer is 104.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Sum of 5 consecutive numbers = 260.

**Formula Used:** Let the five **consecutive numbers** be x, (x + 1), (x + 2), (x + 3), and (x + 4).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3d648d40f5f810e52f613e0c7515e2f59a5dd8fe882fd3f59d58ff823ded8834.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum = x + (x + 1) + (x + 2) + (x + 3) + (x + 4) = 260

⇒ 5x + 10 = 260

⇒ 5x = 260 − 10

⇒ 5x = 250

⇒ x = 50

⇒ First number = x = 50

⇒ Last number = x + 4 = 50 + 4 = 54

⇒ Sum of first and last numbers = 50 + 54 = 104

**∴ The correct answer is 104.**

**__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Progression (AP)

Consecutive numbers form an **Arithmetic Progression** with a common difference of 1. The sum of such a series is given by S = n ÷ 2 × (a + l), where a is the first term and l is the last term.

Middle Term Property

For an odd number of terms (n), the **Average** is exactly equal to the middle term. For a set of 5 numbers, the 3rd number is the average.

Equidistant Sum Rule

In any AP, the sum of terms **equidistant** from the beginning and the end is constant. Thus, First + Last = Second + Second Last = 2 × Middle term.</p

questions.question: When the force and the displacement are in the same direction, then work done will be:
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**positive**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When the **force** and **displacement** are in the same direction, the **angle between force and displacement** is **0 degrees**.
 
• The mathematical expression for **work done** is given as: **Work (W) = Force (F) × Displacement (d) × cos(θ)**, where θ is the angle between the force and displacement.
 
• When θ = 0°, the value of **cos(θ) = 1**, so the formula simplifies to: **W = F × d × 1 = F × d.**
 
• Since both force and displacement are in the same direction, their magnitudes are **positive**, leading to a **positive value for work done**.
 
• This signifies that the energy is being **transferred to the object**, causing displacement in the direction of the applied force.
 
• Examples include pushing a box forward or lifting an object upwards, where the displacement occurs in the same direction as the applied force.

• **Zero**__

 __
 
• If the angle between force and displacement is **90 degrees**, then the **cos(90°) = 0**, resulting in **zero work done**.
 
• This happens when the force does not contribute to the displacement, such as carrying an object horizontally without vertical displacement.
 
 
 
• **Negative**__
 __
 
• If the force and displacement are in **opposite directions**, the angle θ = 180°, and **cos(180°) = -1**, leading to **negative work done**.
 
• Negative work is observed when a force opposes the motion, such as friction slowing down a moving object.
 
 
 
• **Either Positive or Negative**__
 
 
• This option is incorrect as the work done depends on the **specific relationship** between the force and displacement directions.
 
• It cannot be both positive and negative at the same time; it depends on the angle θ.
